freshness_method: All selected IDs are planned as fresh deliberate targets; guarded promotion must independently check them against all canonical Urdu A1, A2, and B1 sequences 1-18 immediately before append.

targets.intended_sense: canal; a water channel used to carry water
targets.external_evidence: Rekhta lists نہر among Urdu meanings of canal and describes an artificial water route.

targets.intended_sense: sample; a small portion taken to examine or represent a larger whole
targets.external_evidence: Rekhta defines نمونہ, among other senses, as a small piece or portion from which the nature or state of something can be learned.

targets.intended_sense: chemical; relating to substances or chemical composition/processes
targets.external_evidence: Rekhta compounds such as کیمیائی مادہ and کیمیائی عمل explicitly use the adjective for chemical substances and processes.

targets.intended_sense: recommendation; a proposal presented as advisable
targets.external_evidence: Rekhta includes the sense of proposing, explaining, or confirming something because it is considered good or necessary.

targets.intended_sense: concern or apprehension about a possible problem
targets.external_evidence: Wiktionary lists Urdu اندیشہ as thought/consideration, apprehension, and anxiety; the learner use is restricted to apprehension/concern.

targets.intended_sense: agreed; sharing the same view on a point
targets.external_evidence: Cambridge's English-Urdu entry for agree gives اتفاق کرنا / متفق ہونا for having the same opinion.

targets.intended_sense: fair or equitable in process or treatment
targets.external_evidence: Rekhta gives منصفانہ as equitable/fair; Cambridge also uses it for fair treatment.
Rekhta defines متنازعہ as something about which there is disagreement or dispute; Cambridge maps controversial to متنازعہ.

targets.intended_sense: exchange; giving and receiving ideas or information
targets.external_evidence: Rekhta's exchange entry lists مبادلہ and describes reciprocal exchange; the passage uses the common phrase خیالات کا مبادلہ.

targets.intended_sense: transfer or movement from one place or route to another
targets.external_evidence: Rekhta's transfer entry gives منتقلی among Urdu meanings for transfer/moving from one place to another.
Rekhta defines کثرت as زیادتی، بہتات and gives abundance/plenty-related senses.

targets.intended_sense: focused or concentrated on one place, time, or point
targets.external_evidence: Rekhta gives focused/concentrated among meanings of مرکوز and describes gathering attention at one point.

targets.intended_sense: application or implementation of a rule or principle in practice
targets.external_evidence: Cambridge's English-Urdu entry for application gives اطلاق / استعمال for putting something to use for a purpose.

targets.intended_sense: license; an official permission or permit to carry out an activity
targets.external_evidence: Cambridge defines licence as an official document giving permission and gives لائسنس / اجازت نامہ in Urdu.

targets.intended_sense: fine or monetary penalty imposed for a rule violation
targets.external_evidence: Rekhta gives جرمانہ as a sum of money exacted by an authority, fine, or penalty.

generation_guardrails: All environmental and municipal scenarios are explicitly constructed/fictional and must not masquerade as real public findings or rules.
P1-P5 introduce exactly three new lexical targets each; P6 introduces none and visibly recycles all fifteen.
All six passages retain ten questions and ten linked answers, with a 220-320 whitespace-token B1 passage band.
Learner-facing title, passage text, questions, and answers use Urdu script only.
Guarded promotion must fail closed on any target-ID freshness collision against prior canonical Urdu.
Generation/integrity status remains separate from educator/publication release approval.
